title: 2025年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is. Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn( 先天的) health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon.

P2 How accurate DNA tests are relies greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait(特征) is. For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease- causing trait is present.

P3 Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities. But saying you are 30 percent East Asian or American hardly reflects your real ancestry.

P4 What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members? There are tools to compare one's DNA with others' to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification. These kinds of applications are generally accurate. It's relatively easy to tell whether two DNA samples belong to close relatives. With distant relatives, results become hazier.

P5 Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary( 遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions. While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. The large majority of our traits and diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others.

P6 Genetic tests for multi-factorial traits are often very tricky to interpret. Height, for example, depends on hundreds of genes, each contributing a little to the outcome, together with a bunch of environmental factors. A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA.

P7 Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak.

questions.q: What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests?
options: Knowing their accuracy.
Evaluating their applicability.
Utilizing the information they provide.
Weighing the consequences they have.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests 直接问文章"说了 什么"，没有 infer/imply 这种推断信号词，是查找型细节题。 51. What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests? A) Knowing their accuracy. B) Evaluating their applicability. C) Utilizing the information they provide. D) Weighing the consequences they have.

【拆句】What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests 主干是 "What does the passage say"，宾语从句省略了 that，完整化即 "the passage say (that) ... is of importance"，regarding genetic tests 是介词短语作话题限定，相当于 about。无陷阱。

【定位】Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon. 无论你是为了构建延伸的 DNA 家谱树而做基因测试，还是想获得关于先天健康状况的精确 信息，搞清楚基因检测到底有多准、我们可以依赖哪些信息，都是很重要的。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are ↔Knowing their accuracy 预判说"知道它准不准"，Knowing their accuracy 一字不差地说"知道它的准确度"，直 接锁定 A。 B) 无中生有 Evaluating their applicability 中的 applicability（适用性/可用性）在 P1 里完全没 提，作者只强调准确度。 C) 偷换概念 what information we can rely upon 说的是"哪些信息可以依赖"——是判断可不可 信，而不是 Utilizing the information they provide 说的"利用它给出的信息"。 D) 无中生有 Weighing the consequences they have 里的 consequences（后果）在原文里没有任 何对应——作者通篇只在谈准确度，没谈"后果"。 什么样的基因检测往往相对可靠？ A) 那些足够复杂以揭示某一特征背后遗传机制的检测。 B) 那些寻找导致某些疾病的特征的检测。 C) 那些专注于所提出的特定问题的检测。 D) 那些寻找由单一基因决定的特征的检测。

questions.q: What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable?
options: Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait.
Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases.
Those focusing on the specific questions being asked.
Those looking for traits determined by a single gene.
questions.explain:
【判型】What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable 是查询事实性比较，找到 原文那句 "X 更可靠" 即可对答案。

【拆句】What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable 中 "tend to be" 是"倾向 于、往往是"的弱化系动词结构，相当于 are usually；comparatively 修饰 reliable，是"相 对来说"，并非"绝对可靠"。 52. What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable? A) Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait. B) Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases. C) Those focusing on the specific questions being asked. D) Those looking for traits determined by a single gene.

【定位】For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease-causing trait is present. 举个例子，对于那些只依赖单个基因的性状，相关检测能给出准确得多的结果，因为你可以 直接看到致病性状到底存不存在。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait 说"复杂到能揭示性状 背后基因"，原文却是"取决于单基因的简单情况更可靠"，方向相反。 B) 偷换概念 Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases 抓住的是 a disease- causing trait——但原文里 "致病性状" 只是"为什么单基因检测可靠"的解释，不是"哪 一类检测可靠"。 C) 偷换概念 Those focusing on the specific questions being asked 把 the specific question you ask 直接搬来，但原文那一句讲的是"准确度取决于问题"，不是"针对特定问题的检 测更可靠"。 D) ✓ 正确 tests for traits that depend on a single gene ↔ Those looking for traits determined by a single gene 全篇只有 single gene 这一处出现"单基因"，且就配着 more reliable，预判和 D 完全 对齐，锁定 D。 从文章中我们了解到关于基因健康检测的什么信息？ A) 它们本身无法识别某些遗传性疾病。 B) 它们通常无法区分遗传因素和非遗传因素。 C) 它们无法独立识别大多数潜在疾病。 D) 它们无法区分生活方式的影响和环境的影响。

questions.q: What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage?
options: They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves.
They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors.
They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases.
They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage 问的是文章"告诉我们 什么"，属于事实查询，不是推断。

【拆句】What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage 句式为 "learn about X from Y"——从 Y 中了解到关于 X 的什么；about 后是话题，from 后是来源。结构平铺直 叙，无陷阱。 53. What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage? A) They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves. B) They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors. C) They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases. D) They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment.

【定位】While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. 虽然某些罕见疾病能轻松识别出来，但大多数潜在的健康问题靠基因检测一项是查不出 来的。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves 用 certain （某些）替换原文的 most（多数）——原文恰恰说 certain rare diseases can be easily identified，让步从句中的 certain rare 反而是"能识别的"，A 把它颠倒了。 B) 无中生有 They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors 凭空加 了"区分基因与非基因因素"这件事——原文只说健康状况受非基因因素影响，从未要求 基因检测"区分"两者。 C) ✓ 正确 most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone ↔ They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases predict 关键的"多数""靠它单独"两个限定词，C 选项用 the majority of 和 independently 一一对应，且主语"基因健康检测"一致，无任何过度信息。 D) 偷换概念 They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment 把 lifestyle 和 environment 单挑出来谈区分，但原文这两词只是 non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others 的举例，且 also 之后从未谈"区 分两者影响"。 是什么使得针对多因素特征的基因检测难以解读？ A) 确定每个单独基因作用的挑战。 B) 预测各种基因如何相互作用的难度。 C) 区分遗传因素和环境因素的难度。 D) 识别所涉及的数百个基因的巨大工作量。

questions.q: What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret?
options: The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene.
The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact.
The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones.
The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved.
questions.explain:
【判型】What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret 是 What makes X Y 的句式，问的是事实层面的原因，原文里有现成原因句。

【拆句】What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret 结构是 "make + 宾语 + 形容词"——"使...变得难以解读"。What 作主语，问的是导致这件难事的原因；to interpret 是后置不定式作形容词补足语。 54. What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret? A) The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene. B) The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact. C) The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones. D) The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved.

【定位】A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. 一次基因检测可以同时查看许多基因，但很难预测这些基因放在一起会怎么"协作"。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene 把"每个单基因的作 用"塞进答案，但 each contributing a little to the outcome 只是顺带一提"每个贡献 一点"，原文并没有说"难以确定每个基因的作用"。 B) ✓ 正确 it's difficult to predict how they will play together ↔ The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact 整篇文章只有 P6 这一句用了 difficult to predict 的结构，预判"基因互动难以预测"严 丝合缝地对应 B 选项的"预测基因如何相互作用的难度"，直接锁定。 C) 无中生有 The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones 编出"区分基因 因素与环境因素"这件事——原文只说"还要把非基因因素也考虑进去"，从未要求"区分 两者"。 D) 无中生有 The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved 把焦点放到"识别 这几百个基因的庞大工作量"——原文 hundreds of genes 只是说数量大，没说"识别它 们工作量巨大"，也根本没说"工作量"才是"难解读"的原因。 文章关于预测性格或天赋的DNA检测说了什么？ A) 它们具有可供应用的坚实科学基础。 B) 它们有助于寻找浪漫伴侣。 C) 它们目前看起来并不乐观。 D) 它们目前没有任何意义。

questions.q: What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents?
options: They are solid scientific bases for application.
They are helpful in finding a romantic match.
They do not look promising at the moment.
They do not make any sense at present.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents——配 合选项里 do not look promising、do not make any sense 这种全是态度评价的格局，本 质是问作者对这件事的态度。

【拆句】What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents 中 "DNA tests to predict ..." 的不定式 to predict 作 DNA tests 的后置定语，等于 "DNA tests that predict ..."——"用来预测人格或才能的 DNA 测试"。 55. What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents? A) They are solid scientific bases for application. B) They are helpful in finding a romantic match. C) They do not look promising at the moment. D) They do not make any sense at present.

【定位】Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak. 那些声称能帮你找到完美恋爱对象的检测、以及那些号称能根据 DNA 预测性格或才能的检 测，都是纯粹的胡说八道。眼下，这些应用的科学依据要么压根不存在，要么薄弱得离谱。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They are solid scientific bases for application 说"是坚实的科学依据"，原文恰好说 the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak ——科学依据要么不存在要么极弱，方向完全相反。 B) 与原文相反 They are helpful in finding a romantic match 抓了原文里的另一个例子 find your perfect romantic match——但原文是把它当作"也是胡说"的反面例子，B 却说它"有帮 助"，立场反了。 C) 偷换概念 They do not look promising at the moment 译过来是"目前看起来不太有前景"—— 但原文是 pure nonsense（纯属胡扯），属于强烈否定，C 把它弱化成"前景不佳"这种 中性偏负的客气说法。 D) ✓ 正确 are pure nonsense ↔They do not make any sense at present At the moment ↔at present 预判"作者强烈否定"对应 do not make any sense；at present 又把 at the moment 这个时间限定带上了——D 一字不漏地把作者的核心态度搬过来了。
